title: Given an unsorted array of integers and a value K, return the Kth largest element (by value, not the Kth distinct element).
shortTitle: Kth Largest Element in an Array: min-heap of size K or QuickSelect
keyPoints: Size-K min-heap: push each element, poll when size exceeds K; the root is the Kth largest after one pass.
Min-heap approach runs in O(n log K) time with O(K) space and works for streaming data.
QuickSelect: partition like quicksort but recurse into only the side containing the target rank; average O(n) time.
QuickSelect mutates the array and has O(n^2) worst case; randomize the pivot to avoid it.
The heap is preferred for streaming; QuickSelect is preferred for in-memory batch computation.
This is finding the element at index n-K in ascending sorted order.

s1_definition.oneliner: Keep a size-K min-heap whose root is the Kth largest, or use QuickSelect to partition toward the target rank in average O(n).
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Min-heap of size K** – maintains only the K largest elements; the root (smallest of those) is the Kth largest. O(n log K) time, O(K) space.
- **QuickSelect** – partitions the array around a pivot and recurses into only the side containing the target index. Average O(n) time, O(1) extra space.
- **Randomized pivot** – prevents worst-case O(n^2) in QuickSelect by choosing a random pivot.
- **Streaming vs batch** – heap works for streaming; QuickSelect needs the full array in memory.
s1_definition.analogy: At the National Bank of India, the risk desk sets a daily alert threshold from the Kth largest transaction amount. The heap approach keeps a shortlist of exactly K biggest amounts; whenever a bigger amount arrives, it bumps out the smallest on the shortlist. QuickSelect splits amounts into bigger and smaller piles and keeps narrowing to the pile containing the rank you want.

sections.s6_takeaway:
Finding the Kth largest element has two strong solutions. The size-K min-heap keeps only the K largest elements: push each element, poll when the heap exceeds K, and the root is the Kth largest. This runs in O(n log K) and is ideal for streaming data.

QuickSelect reframes the problem as finding the element at index n-K in ascending order. Partition around a random pivot, discard the side that cannot contain the target, and recurse into the correct side. Average time is O(n), but a bad pivot sequence degrades to O(n^2), so always randomize.

The trade-off is clear: heap is simple, worst-case predictable, streaming-friendly, and non-destructive. QuickSelect is faster on average but mutates the array and needs the full data in memory.

At the National Bank of India, the risk desk set a daily alert threshold from the Kth largest transaction. Amounts streamed in all day, so Rajesh used the min-heap, keeping only K values at any moment. QuickSelect was the option for batch recomputation over a finished day's data.

Remember one sentence: a size-K min-heap keeps the K largest elements, and its root is the Kth largest after one pass.
